answer: Rate-limiting nullifiers deter Sybils using staked deposits and zero-knowledge Shamir secret sharing. An agent locks funds in a Merkle tree and sends a proof plus a key share per action, say bidding on copper or pigment lots. Exceeding an epoch quota reuses a line slope across messages, letting verifiers recover the key and slash the stake. Attackers must commit capital per identity rather than hollow clones, though wealthy actors can fund extra stakes.
